operative_text.controlling:
3.55   Except when the context or these rules otherwise provide, a
rule that applies to or in respect of
(a) a plaintiff applies equally to or in respect of a third party
plaintiff,
(b) a defendant applies equally to or in respect of a third party
defendant, and
(c) a pleading related to a claim made by a statement of claim
applies equally to or in respect of a pleading related to a
third party claim.

carrier_notes.BOOK_C:
*[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 3.55 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*

Subdivision 7: COUNTERCLAIMS

BOOK_A.title: Application of Rules toThird Party Claims
BOOK_A.defined_terms: defendant, plaintiff, pleading, rules, third party defendant, third party plaintiff A third party notice is a pleading, and must recite facts giving a cause of action, just as a statement of claim must. Part of a third party notice raising a claim outside the limitation period shouldbe "struck." Another part shown by affidavit to be hopeless should be struck too. Third party notices can be summarily dismissed. But it takes a clear case to strike out a third party notice. A third party notice can be struck out if it does not disclose a cause of action by the defendant against the third party. The tests would be those under R.3.68.Presumably the court would also strike it out if it violated R.3.45 and no time extension were given. A grant of summary judgment, even on a third party notice, is entitled to considerable deference on appeal. The Rules on formal offers and double costs to successful defendants who beat their own offers, apply to third party notices and offers by third parties. Case law on whether a third party can counterclaim is unclear, but if he can, he has to name the person issuing the third party notice as a defendant by counterclaim.A counterclaim was struck for want of that. This Rule still appears not to allow an amendment to a counterclaimto add an extra plaintiff by counterclaim so far completely unrelated to the lawsuit. On costs, see R.3.46 n. *Subdivision 7 Counterclaims *Right to Counterclaim *

BOOK_A.commentary_review_flag: Read in full, p.3-123 (line 3477) to p.3-124 (line 3506): rule text (in pieces), Defined Terms 'defendant, plaintiff, pleading, rules, third party defendant, third party plaintiff' (the Appendix defines each), no Related Provisions, and a note of five paragraphs, with footnotes 2-10 and 1 as printed. The built record: the Defined Terms line and the whole note are in defined_terms (after the terms, the note paragraphs, then the heading of Subdivision 7 'Counterclaims' and the title of 3.56 'Right to Counterclaim'); related_provisions and commentary are empty; the raw-text field held the footnote blocks (kept in the text note); nothing dropped. The note is the target of the pointer 'See R.3.55 n. below' in the 3.45 note (p.3-116 line 3271); the 3.45 note sentence is 'See R.3.55 n.below' with no statement attached. (1) Statements read against the official text: 'A third party notice is a pleading' agrees with 3.55(c) (a pleading related to a claim made by a statement of claim applies equally to a pleading related to a third party claim); 'The tests would be those under R.3.68' and 'the court would also strike it out if it violated R.3.45 and no time extension were given' land on official 3.68 and 3.45 (not re-read here for the tests); 'The Rules on formal offers and double costs to successful defendants who beat their own offers, apply to third party notices and offers by third parties' is a reading of 3.55(a)-(b) (Part 4 rules on formal offers not re-read here); 'Case law on whether a third party can counterclaim is unclear, but if he can, he has to name the person issuing the third party notice as a defendant by counterclaim' - official 3.56(2) says a third party defendant may, by counterclaim, file a claim against the plaintiff, defendant or third party plaintiff, or any combination of them, with or without any other person, and does not say the person issuing the third party notice must be named; 'On costs, see R.3.46 n.' lands on the costs paragraphs of the 3.46 note. (2) Other rules' pointers to 3.55: Book A p.3-116 (line 3271) 'See R.3.55 n. below'; the 3.48 related provision '3.55 (status of parties on third party claims)' (p.3-120, line 3421; official title 'Application of rules to third party claims'); R.5 p.5-89 (line 4770) 'See Rr.3.46 and 3.55'; R.7 p.7-41 (line 2159) '... it under R.3.55.' (a footnote number is run into the text; the rest of the sentence was not opened). (3) The cases in the footnotes (C.D.I.C. v. Prisco, Stolk v. 382779 Alta. 2002 ABQB 360, MacKay v. Farm Bus. Consult. 2006 ABCA 316, Tollestrup, Agrium v. Chubb 2002 ABQB 495, Wenzel v. Desanti 2011 ABCA 226, Breen v. Foremost Ind. 2022 ABQB 478, and others) were not checked; Book A prints 'C.D.I.C. v. Prisco (CA) [1998] 3 WWR 256, 206 AR 290' here (fn 2) is printed '9Northland Bank v. Willson (C.D.I.C. v. Barker) (CA) [1998] 3 WWR 256, 206 AR 290' in the 3.45 note (p.3-116 line 3265) - the same reporter cite under two different case names (Prisco / Barker).
